nodes.name: Pulsed Laser Deposition on STO(100)
nodes.procedure: The epitaxial PBCO thin films were grown on the single-crystal (100)-oriented SrTiO3 (STO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition using a KrF excimer laser of 248 nm wavelength. All of the films were fabricated under an oxygen pressure of 250 mTorr with a laser repetition rate of 5 Hz at an energy density of 2 J/cm² at a substrate temperature of 610°C using a ceramic PBCO target material (99.99%). After deposition, all films were annealed at 600°C under pure oxygen (300 Torr) for 30 min and then cooled down to room temperature at a rate of 5°C/min. For convenience, the samples grown on (100)-oriented substrates are marked PBCO(100).

nodes.characterization_summary: All PBCO films grow as single crystal with well-defined Kiessig fringes; rocking curve FWHM of 0.03°, 0.11°, and 0.21° for (100), (110), and (111) orientations respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures 1a and S1, all films grow along with the crystal faces of a single-crystal substrate with well-defined Kiessig fringes... The rocking curve measurement (Figure S2a) from the (100), (110), and (111) reflections of the PBCO films have a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.03, 0.11, and 0.21°, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: All PBCO films have similar thickness of ~35 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRR (Figure 1b) shows that all films have a similar thickness (~35 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: RSM shows films are coherently strained with out-of-plane lattice parameters of 7.712, 5.478, and 4.462 Å for (100), (110), and (111) orientations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1c, it displays almost the same in-plane lattice parameters as the substrate because all films are coherently strained. Analysis yields out-of-plane lattice parameters of 7.712, 5.478, and 4.462 Å for the (100), (110), and (111) orientations, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: PBCO films show smooth surface with root-mean-square roughness less than 0.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphology was captured by AFM (Figures 1d and S1b), showing a smooth surface with root-mean-square roughness of less than 0.3 nm.

properties.description: Height profile of nanostructured surface showing fibrous or sheet-like morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and SAED confirm high crystalline quality and epitaxial growth of PBCO films on STO substrates with 112-type pseudocubic superlattice structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To gain further insight into the epitaxial behavior and interface structure of the as-grown PBCO films, TEM, and SAED measurements were performed... The results indicate that the PBCO films are of high crystalline quality and epitaxially grown on STO substrates.

nodes.characterization_summary: No noticeable binding energy shifts for Co 2p, Ba 2p, Co 3p, Pr 3d core levels across orientations, indicating similar Co valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There are no noticeable binding energy shifts for the Co 2p, Ba 2p, Co 3p, and Pr 3d core level spectra (Figures 2a and S4), suggesting a similar Co valence state and surface composition in different-orientation films.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co L-edge XAS (TEY mode) shows consistent Co³⁺ valence but higher HS Co³⁺ peak intensity at ~778.4 eV for PBCO(100); O K-edge shows increasing t₂g unoccupied states (~527.7 eV) and decreasing eg unoccupied states (~528.8 eV) from PBCO(111) to PBCO(100), confirming higher HS Co³⁺ content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HS Co³⁺ peak intensity at ∼778.4 eV of PBCO(100) is higher than that of PBCO(110) and PBCO(111)... the normalized O K-edge XAS display (Figure 2d) two broader features at ∼527.7 and 528.8 eV... the intensity of the feature at ∼527.7 eV gradually increases, while the feature at 528.8 eV decreases from PBCO(111) to PBCO(100).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-plane magnetic hysteresis shows spontaneous magnetic moments per Co atom of ~1.47, ~0.4, and ~0.15 μB/f.u. for PBCO(100), (110), and (111), indicating higher HS Co³⁺ proportion in PBCO(100).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spontaneous magnetic moment per Co atom for PBCO(100), PBCO(110), and PBCO(111) orientation are ~1.47, ~0.4, and ~0.15 μB/f.u., respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl of 71.3, 94.5, and 74.6 μF/cm² for PBCO(100), (110), and (111), consistent with smooth oxide surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PBCO(100), PBCO(110), and PBCO(111) exhibit Cdl of approximately 71.3, 94.5, and 74.6 μFcm², respectively, which is consistent with a specific capacitance of 60 μFcm² on an ideal flat oxide surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: VB XPS shows hybridized Co 3d-O 2p states with metallic character (density of states near EF) for all PBCO films.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the VB spectra of PBCO films consist of two features: A and B, resulting from the hybridized states of occupied Co 3d and O 2p. A certain density of electronic states near the EF is observed for all films, indicating that all films are metallic.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in [Fe(CN)6]³⁻/⁴⁻ shows excellent surface electronic conduction ability for all PBCO films.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Before OER performance testing, the charge transport behavior of different-orientation films was examined by outer-sphere redox couple [Fe(CN)6]³⁻/⁴⁻ measurements (Figure S6), showing the excellent surface electronic conduction ability for all films.
